ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A double pulley is free to rotate about its axis through its center. The radii of the two pulleys are $R$ and $2R$. Two cords are wrapped in opposite directions on the pulleys and are attached to masses. As a result, the two tension forces acting on the pulley are equal and acting downwards as shown in the image below so that $F_1 = 2F_2$. When released from rest, what will be the direction of the angular acceleration?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a coaxial double pulley, with the inner small pulley labeled as radius R and the outer large pulley labeled as radius 2R. On the left side there is a rope along the tangent of the small pulley downward, with the applied force labeled F1; on the right side there is a rope along the tangent of the large pulley downward, with the applied force labeled F2. The two ropes pull downward on the two sides of the pulley, therefore producing torques in opposite directions about the rotation axis. Reasoning: The magnitude of the torque of each tension about the central axis is equal to the force multiplied by the corresponding pulley radius. On the left side, F1 acts on the small pulley of radius R, so tau1 = F1 R. On the right side, F2 acts on the large pulley of radius 2R, so tau2 = F2(2R). The problem gives F1 = 2F2, therefore tau1 = (2F2)R = 2F2R, while tau2 = 2F2R. The two torques have equal magnitudes but opposite directions, so the resultant torque is 0. From tau_net = I alpha, alpha = 0 can be obtained.

raw_record.question_text: A double pulley is free to rotate about its axis through its center. The radii of the two pulleys are $R$ and $2R$. Two cords are wrapped in opposite directions on the pulleys and are attached to masses. As a result, the two tension forces acting on the pulley are equal and acting downwards as shown in the image below so that $F_1 = 2F_2$. When released from rest, what will be the direction of the angular acceleration?

method.method_draft: Use a direct torque-balance route. From the image, note that F1 acts downward on the left side of the smaller pulley, whose radius is R, while F2 acts downward on the right side of the larger pulley, whose radius is 2R. The cords are tangent to their pulleys, so each force produces a torque of magnitude force times pulley radius. Because the forces act on opposite sides and the cords are wrapped in opposite directions, their torques have opposite signs. From the text, use F1 = 2F2. Then compare magnitudes: tau1 = F1 R = 2F2 R and tau2 = F2(2R) = 2F2 R. Since the opposite torques are equal in magnitude, net torque is zero, so by tau_net = I alpha, alpha = 0. Therefore there is no angular acceleration.
